title: Casarecce with Sausage
subtitle: Twisted pasta with crumbled Italian sausage and tomato
excerpt: Crumbled pork sausage and a simple tomato sauce cling inside the scrolled ridges of casarecce. A weeknight supper that tastes far richer than its short cook time suggests.
sourceNotes: Classic Sicilian treatment of casarecce with pork sausage and tomato, adapted for a standard hob.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The sauce can be made a day ahead and reheated. Cook pasta fresh.

content.text: Casarecce is a short scrolled pasta that holds a chunky sauce well. Crumble the sausage finely so it coats every piece. Keep the heat steady so the sauce reduces without catching on the base.
Warm the olive oil in the frying pan over a medium heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crumble the sausage into the pan. Break it into small pieces with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5 minutes until browned all over.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Crush the tomatoes with the spoon. Simmer for 12 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta for 1 minute less than the packet says.
Scoop out a mugful of pasta water. Drain the pasta and tip it into the sauce.
Toss well over a low heat for 1 minute. Add a splash of pasta water if the sauce is too thick. Serve with parmesan and basil.

items.cause: The tomatoes reduced too fast on a high heat.
items.fix: Add pasta water a little at a time and toss to loosen.

items.symptom: The sausage is grey rather than browned.
items.cause: The pan was too cool or overcrowded.
items.fix: Spread the meat in a single layer and resist stirring for 2 minutes before breaking it up.

items.cause: It sat in the colander too long without sauce.
items.fix: Add it to the sauce straight from draining and toss immediately.
